# Replace git submodules with an auto-cloned sibling checkout

## Context and Problem Statement

Since 2023-06-15 the external skill repositories had been vendored as git
submodules, recorded in
[DR-0002](DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules.md). That arrangement
left a fresh clone incomplete: the submodule directories were empty until
someone remembered to run a submodule init, and a coding agent pointed at such a
clone would find no external skills at all.

Nine months later the mechanism was removed outright. The commit subject names
the goal directly: *"so a fresh clone needs no submodule init"*.

## Forces and Constraints

- A fresh clone must be usable without a git-specific initialisation step that a newcomer will forget.
- The external history must stay out of this repository, which `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh` states in its own header comment.
- The setup step has to be safe to repeat, since a newcomer will not know whether it has already run.

## Considered Options

### An auto-cloned sibling checkout

A single script, `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh`, clones each external
repository next to this one. It resolves the parent directory of the repository,
iterates a hard-coded list of `community-skills` and `partner-skills`, and skips
any that is already present:

```bash
for repo in community-skills partner-skills; do
  [ -d "$SIBLINGS/$repo" ] || git clone "https://example.com/$repo.git" "$SIBLINGS/$repo"
done
```

**Pros**
- A fresh clone needs one documented command, and the README says so in two lines.
- The script is idempotent because of the `[ -d ... ] ||` guard, so re-running it is harmless.
- The external history stays outside this repository, which was the one property worth keeping from the submodule arrangement.

**Cons**
- Nothing pins the external revision any more. The script clones the default branch, so the reproducibility that motivated DR-0002 is given up.
- The external skills now live outside the repository boundary, so nothing in a diff here shows which revision an agent actually ran against.
- The repository list is hard-coded in the script rather than declared in a manifest.

### Git submodules, the incumbent

Described in [DR-0002](DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules.md), and
rejected here.

**Pros**
- The external revision is pinned and reviewable.

**Cons**
- A fresh clone is unusable until a submodule init has run, which is the failure this decision set out to remove.

## Decision

In the context of external skill repositories that a fresh clone had to be able
to reach, facing submodule directories that stayed empty until someone ran a
submodule init, we decided for **an auto-cloned sibling checkout driven by
`scripts/clone_external_skills.sh`** (inferred from history) and against **git
submodules**, to achieve a clone that becomes usable through one ordinary,
repeatable command, accepting that the external revisions are no longer pinned
and that the effective versions are no longer visible in this repository's
history.

### Consequences

Onboarding got shorter. The README now carries the whole setup instruction:
run `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh` once after a clone.

Reproducibility was traded away. DR-0002 existed precisely to pin the external
revisions, and this decision removes that pin without replacing it; the
`*-workspace/` entry in `.gitignore` suggests the sibling checkouts are treated
as scratch space rather than as controlled inputs. Anyone who later needs a
reproducible agent run will have to reintroduce pinning, most likely as a
revision pinned inside the script or in a small manifest beside it.

The `example.com` clone URLs in the script are placeholders, so the script as
committed cannot succeed against a real remote without editing.

# Replace git submodules with an auto-cloned sibling checkout

## Context and Problem Statement

Since 2023-06-15 the external skill repositories had been vendored as git
submodules, recorded in
[DR-0002](DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules.md). That arrangement
left a fresh clone incomplete: the submodule directories were empty until
someone remembered to run a submodule init, and a coding agent pointed at such a
clone would find no external skills at all.

Nine months later the mechanism was removed outright. The commit subject names
the goal directly: *"so a fresh clone needs no submodule init"*.

## Forces and Constraints

- A fresh clone must be usable without a git-specific initialisation step that a newcomer will forget.
- The external history must stay out of this repository, which `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh` states in its own header comment.
- The setup step has to be safe to repeat, since a newcomer will not know whether it has already run.

## Considered Options

### An auto-cloned sibling checkout

A single script, `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh`, clones each external
repository next to this one. It resolves the parent directory of the repository,
iterates a hard-coded list of `community-skills` and `partner-skills`, and skips
any that is already present:

```bash
for repo in community-skills partner-skills; do
  [ -d "$SIBLINGS/$repo" ] || git clone "https://example.com/$repo.git" "$SIBLINGS/$repo"
done
```

**Pros**
- A fresh clone needs one documented command, and the README says so in two lines.
- The script is idempotent because of the `[ -d ... ] ||` guard, so re-running it is harmless.
- The external history stays outside this repository, which was the one property worth keeping from the submodule arrangement.

**Cons**
- Nothing pins the external revision any more. The script clones the default branch, so the reproducibility that motivated DR-0002 is given up.
- The external skills now live outside the repository boundary, so nothing in a diff here shows which revision an agent actually ran against.
- The repository list is hard-coded in the script rather than declared in a manifest.

### Git submodules, the incumbent

Described in [DR-0002](DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules.md), and
rejected here.

**Pros**
- The external revision is pinned and reviewable.

**Cons**
- A fresh clone is unusable until a submodule init has run, which is the failure this decision set out to remove.

## Decision

In the context of external skill repositories that a fresh clone had to be able
to reach, facing submodule directories that stayed empty until someone ran a
submodule init, we decided for **an auto-cloned sibling checkout driven by
`scripts/clone_external_skills.sh`** (inferred from history) and against **git
submodules**, to achieve a clone that becomes usable through one ordinary,
repeatable command, accepting that the external revisions are no longer pinned
and that the effective versions are no longer visible in this repository's
history.

### Consequences

Onboarding got shorter. The README now carries the whole setup instruction:
run `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh` once after a clone.

Reproducibility was traded away. DR-0002 existed precisely to pin the external
revisions, and this decision removes that pin without replacing it; the
`*-workspace/` entry in `.gitignore` suggests the sibling checkouts are treated
as scratch space rather than as controlled inputs. Anyone who later needs a
reproducible agent run will have to reintroduce pinning, most likely as a
revision pinned inside the script or in a small manifest beside it.

The `example.com` clone URLs in the script are placeholders, so the script as
committed cannot succeed against a real remote without editing.

## More Information

Evidence commits:

- `86354b8` (2023-06-15) — feat: vendored external skills as git submodules to pin their revisions
- `b6590d7` (2024-03-11) — feat: replaced git submodules with an auto-cloned sibling checkout so a fresh clone needs no submodule init

Supersedes [DR-0002](DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules.md).

## What I could and couldn't do

This session has no Bash tool, so I could not run `git log`, `git show`, or `git ls-tree`. Instead I mined `.git/logs/HEAD` — the reflog — which records every one of the 7 commits on `main` with its hash, author, timestamp, and subject, and cross-checked each against the current working tree. The root commit is present and marked `commit (initial)`, so the history is complete, not shallow.

The gap this leaves: **I never saw a diff.** Every claim below traces to a commit subject or to a file in the tree today, never to the contents of a change. Where a commit subject asserts something I could not verify by reading files, I say so in the DR.

## Triage

| # | Proposed DR title | Date | Evidence | Confidence | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Vendor external skills as git submodules to pin their revisions | 2023-06 | `86354b8` subject states the decision and its reason; `dc25654` bumps "the pinned submodule revisions", confirming submodules existed | high | **written as DR-0002** · pair: reversed by #2 |
| 2 | Replace git submodules with an auto-cloned sibling checkout | 2024-03 | `b6590d7` subject; `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh`, README post-clone line, `.gitignore` `*-workspace/`, no `.gitmodules` in tree | high | **written as DR-0003** · pair: reverses #1 |
| 3 | One plugin per domain | 2023-07 | `97684ee` | — | already recorded in DR-0001 — excluded |
| 4 | Pin the markdownlint version | 2024-05 | `70d7483`; `.github-linter.json` holds `{"markdownlint": "0.33.0"}` | low | lint-tooling commit, a counter-signal; no observable trade-off — **not written** |

`dc25654` (submodule bump) and `e1d896b` (README typo) are routine and were folded into the evidence rather than proposed as decisions.

You told me not to stop, so I wrote the two high-confidence candidates — the triage default — and skipped #4 rather than write a speculative DR. If you want #4 recorded, say so and it becomes DR-0004.

## Files written

| Path | Title | Status | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skills-repo/docs/decisions/DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules.md` | Vendor external skills as git submodules to pin their revisions | superseded by DR-0003 | 2023-06-15 |
| `skills-repo/docs/decisions/DR-0003-replace-submodules-with-auto-cloned-sibling-checkout.md` | Replace git submodules with an auto-cloned sibling checkout | adopted | 2024-03-11 |

Both cross-link each other. Numbering continues DR-0001's `DR-NNNN-kebab-title.md` scheme, in chronological order of the decision.

One formatting judgment call: DR-0001 uses a `# DR-0001 — Title` heading with a Status/Date/Deciders bullet list, not the YAML frontmatter of the log-decision template. I matched DR-0001 so the log reads as one document set, and used the template's section structure inside. Tell me if you'd rather have the frontmatter form and I'll convert all three.

## My questions

1. **Is the loss of revision pinning in DR-0003 known and accepted?** The clone script runs a bare `git clone` with no ref, so it fetches whatever the default branch holds. That discards exactly the guarantee DR-0002 was created to obtain. The history shows the trade being made but never shows it being weighed. If it was an oversight rather than a choice, DR-0003's "accepting" clause is the sentence to fix.
2. **Was the markdownlint pin (`70d7483`, two months later) a response to that?** I noted the coincidence in DR-0003 and explicitly marked it unverified. You can either confirm it, or I should delete that paragraph — it's the weakest inference in either file.
3. **Was there a rejected alternative in 2023?** DR-0002 carries the honest note that alternatives weren't documented. If a vendored copy or a package registry was discussed and dismissed, that's the one thing the history genuinely cannot recover.

These are reconstructions from commit subjects, so a human review pass is worth the time — particularly on the two Y-statements, which are the parts I inferred rather than read. Worth committing as `docs: backfilled DR-0002 and DR-0003 from git history`.

- Status: superseded by DR-0003
- Date: 2023-06-15
- Deciders: Jamie Rivera

## Context and Problem Statement

Six weeks after the repository was created, it needed skills that live in
repositories outside this one. Those repositories move on their own schedule, so
consuming them at their moving tip would have let an upstream change alter the
behaviour of this repository without any commit here.

The problem was therefore how to consume external skill repositories while
keeping the exact revision in use visible and reproducible from this
repository's own history.

## Forces and Constraints

- External skill repositories are owned elsewhere and change without notice.
- The revision in use has to be recorded in this repository, so that a checkout
  of an old commit here reproduces the skills as they were then.
- Git offers submodules for exactly this, with no extra tooling to build or
  maintain.

## Considered Options

### Git submodules pinned to a revision

Reference each external skill repository as a submodule, so the parent
repository stores the commit SHA of every external repository.

**Pros**
- The pinned revision is recorded in this repository and moves only in an
  explicit commit, which `dc25654` shows was the intended workflow.
- No custom tooling: the mechanism is built into git.
- Checking out an old commit here reproduces the matching external revisions.

**Cons**
- A fresh clone is not usable until `git submodule update --init` has run, a
  cost that `b6590d7` later named explicitly as the reason to undo this
  decision.
- Every revision bump is a commit in this repository, which is visible
  maintenance work.

Alternatives considered at the time were not documented.

## Decision

In the context of consuming skill repositories owned outside this repository,
facing the risk that an upstream change silently alters behaviour here, we
decided for **git submodules pinned to a revision** (inferred from history), to
achieve a reproducible and explicitly recorded external revision, accepting that
a fresh clone needs a submodule init step before it works and that each bump
costs a commit here.

### Consequences

The external revision in use became visible in this repository's history, and
moving it became a deliberate act. `dc25654` is that act performed once.

Cloning the repository stopped being a single step. That cost was carried for
roughly nine months, until DR-0003 traded the pinning away to remove it.

## More Information

Evidence:

- `c1f032d` (2023-05-04) — chore: initial commit
- `86354b8` (2023-06-15) — feat: vendored external skills as git submodules to pin their revisions
- `dc25654` (2023-09-19) — chore: bumped the pinned submodule revisions

- Status: superseded by DR-0003
- Date: 2023-06-15
- Deciders: Jamie Rivera

## Context and Problem Statement

Six weeks after the repository was created, it needed skills that live in
repositories outside this one. Those repositories move on their own schedule, so
consuming them at their moving tip would have let an upstream change alter the
behaviour of this repository without any commit here.

The problem was therefore how to consume external skill repositories while
keeping the exact revision in use visible and reproducible from this
repository's own history.

## Forces and Constraints

- External skill repositories are owned elsewhere and change without notice.
- The revision in use has to be recorded in this repository, so that a checkout
  of an old commit here reproduces the skills as they were then.
- Git offers submodules for exactly this, with no extra tooling to build or
  maintain.

## Considered Options

### Git submodules pinned to a revision

Reference each external skill repository as a submodule, so the parent
repository stores the commit SHA of every external repository.

**Pros**
- The pinned revision is recorded in this repository and moves only in an
  explicit commit, which `dc25654` shows was the intended workflow.
- No custom tooling: the mechanism is built into git.
- Checking out an old commit here reproduces the matching external revisions.

**Cons**
- A fresh clone is not usable until `git submodule update --init` has run, a
  cost that `b6590d7` later named explicitly as the reason to undo this
  decision.
- Every revision bump is a commit in this repository, which is visible
  maintenance work.

Alternatives considered at the time were not documented.

## Decision

In the context of consuming skill repositories owned outside this repository,
facing the risk that an upstream change silently alters behaviour here, we
decided for **git submodules pinned to a revision** (inferred from history), to
achieve a reproducible and explicitly recorded external revision, accepting that
a fresh clone needs a submodule init step before it works and that each bump
costs a commit here.

### Consequences

The external revision in use became visible in this repository's history, and
moving it became a deliberate act. `dc25654` is that act performed once.

Cloning the repository stopped being a single step. That cost was carried for
roughly nine months, until DR-0003 traded the pinning away to remove it.

## More Information

Evidence:

- `c1f032d` (2023-05-04) — chore: initial commit
- `86354b8` (2023-06-15) — feat: vendored external skills as git submodules to pin their revisions
- `dc25654` (2023-09-19) — chore: bumped the pinned submodule revisions

Superseded by [DR-0003-replace-submodules-with-auto-cloned-sibling-checkout](DR-0003-replace-submodules-with-auto-cloned-sibling-checkout.md).

- Status: adopted
- Date: 2024-03-11
- Deciders: Jamie Rivera

## Context and Problem Statement

External skills had been consumed as pinned git submodules since 2023-06-15, as
recorded in [DR-0002](DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules.md). A
fresh clone of this repository was therefore incomplete until
`git submodule update --init` had been run, and the history of the external
repositories was pulled into this one.

The commit that made the change states the driving concern in its own subject:
a fresh clone should need no submodule init.

## Forces and Constraints

- A fresh clone should be usable without a submodule step.
- The history of the external repositories should stay out of this repository.
- Whatever replaces submodules has to be a single, repeatable command, since
  the README has to be able to instruct a newcomer in one line.

## Considered Options

### Git submodules pinned to a revision

The arrangement in place since DR-0002.

**Pros**
- Records the exact external revision in this repository's history.
- Built into git, so there is nothing to maintain.

**Cons**
- A fresh clone needs `git submodule update --init` before it works.
- Pulls external history into this repository.

### An auto-cloned sibling checkout

A script, `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh`, clones each external repository
next to this one, and skips any that is already present. The README instructs
the reader to run it once after cloning, and `.gitignore` excludes the
`*-workspace/` directories that result.

**Pros**
- Idempotent: the `[ -d ... ] ||` guard makes a re-run a no-op, so the script is
  safe to run at any time.
- The external history stays in the sibling repositories, out of this one.
- The clone of this repository is complete on its own; the external skills are
  fetched by a plain, readable shell script rather than by submodule mechanics.

**Cons**
- The revision is no longer pinned. The script runs a bare
  `git clone https://example.com/$repo.git` with no ref, so every developer gets
  whatever the default branch holds at the moment they run it. This is the
  guarantee that DR-0002 was written to obtain.
- The post-clone step did not disappear, it changed shape: the README still
  asks the reader to run one command after cloning.
- The external repository list is hard-coded in the script.

## Decision

In the context of external skills consumed as pinned submodules, facing a fresh
clone that did not work until a submodule init had been run, we decided for **an
auto-cloned sibling checkout** (inferred from history) and against **git
submodules**, to achieve a clone that carries none of the external history and a
single idempotent command to fetch it, accepting that the external revision is
no longer pinned and that a manual post-clone step remains.

### Consequences

The repository no longer records which revision of an external skill repository
is in use, so a checkout of an old commit here no longer reproduces the external
skills as they were then. This is a deliberate reversal of DR-0002, and it is
the main risk this decision carries.

Two months later, `70d7483` pinned the markdownlint version in
`.github-linter.json`. The history does not link the two, so the connection is
unverified, but it is the only other pinning in the repository.

## More Information

Evidence:

- `b6590d7` (2024-03-11) — feat: replaced git submodules with an auto-cloned sibling checkout so a fresh clone needs no submodule init
- `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh` — the idempotent clone loop over `community-skills` and `partner-skills`
- `README.md` — "External skills are cloned as sibling repositories. Run `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh` once after a clone."
- `.gitignore` — the `*-workspace/` entry
- No `.gitmodules` remains in the tree

Supersedes [DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules](DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules.md).

The gap this leaves: **I never saw a diff.** Every claim below traces to a commit subject or to a file in the tree today, never to the contents of a change. Where a commit subject asserts something I could not verify by reading files, I say so in the DR.

## Triage

| # | Proposed DR title | Date | Evidence | Confidence | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Vendor external skills as git submodules to pin their revisions | 2023-06 | `86354b8` subject states the decision and its reason; `dc25654` bumps "the pinned submodule revisions", confirming submodules existed | high | **written as DR-0002** · pair: reversed by #2 |
| 2 | Replace git submodules with an auto-cloned sibling checkout | 2024-03 | `b6590d7` subject; `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh`, README post-clone line, `.gitignore` `*-workspace/`, no `.gitmodules` in tree | high | **written as DR-0003** · pair: reverses #1 |
| 3 | One plugin per domain | 2023-07 | `97684ee` | — | already recorded in DR-0001 — excluded |
| 4 | Pin the markdownlint version | 2024-05 | `70d7483`; `.github-linter.json` holds `{"markdownlint": "0.33.0"}` | low | lint-tooling commit, a counter-signal; no observable trade-off — **not written** |

`dc25654` (submodule bump) and `e1d896b` (README typo) are routine and were folded into the evidence rather than proposed as decisions.

You told me not to stop, so I wrote the two high-confidence candidates — the triage default — and skipped #4 rather than write a speculative DR. If you want #4 recorded, say so and it becomes DR-0004.

## Files written

| Path | Title | Status | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skills-repo/docs/decisions/DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules.md` | Vendor external skills as git submodules to pin their revisions | superseded by DR-0003 | 2023-06-15 |
| `skills-repo/docs/decisions/DR-0003-replace-submodules-with-auto-cloned-sibling-checkout.md` | Replace git submodules with an auto-cloned sibling checkout | adopted | 2024-03-11 |

Both cross-link each other. Numbering continues DR-0001's `DR-NNNN-kebab-title.md` scheme, in chronological order of the decision.

One formatting judgment call: DR-0001 uses a `# DR-0001 — Title` heading with a Status/Date/Deciders bullet list, not the YAML frontmatter of the log-decision template. I matched DR-0001 so the log reads as one document set, and used the template's section structure inside. Tell me if you'd rather have the frontmatter form and I'll convert all three.

## My questions

1. **Is the loss of revision pinning in DR-0003 known and accepted?** The clone script runs a bare `git clone` with no ref, so it fetches whatever the default branch holds. That discards exactly the guarantee DR-0002 was created to obtain. The history shows the trade being made but never shows it being weighed. If it was an oversight rather than a choice, DR-0003's "accepting" clause is the sentence to fix.
2. **Was the markdownlint pin (`70d7483`, two months later) a response to that?** I noted the coincidence in DR-0003 and explicitly marked it unverified. You can either confirm it, or I should delete that paragraph — it's the weakest inference in either file.
3. **Was there a rejected alternative in 2023?** DR-0002 carries the honest note that alternatives weren't documented. If a vendored copy or a package registry was discussed and dismissed, that's the one thing the history genuinely cannot recover.

These are reconstructions from commit subjects, so a human review pass is worth the time — particularly on the two Y-statements, which are the parts I inferred rather than read. Worth committing as `docs: backfilled DR-0002 and DR-0003 from git history`.

## Context and Problem Statement

Six weeks after the repository was created, it needed skills that live in
repositories outside this one. Those repositories move on their own schedule, so
consuming them at their moving tip would have let an upstream change alter the
behaviour of this repository without any commit here.

The problem was therefore how to consume external skill repositories while
keeping the exact revision in use visible and reproducible from this
repository's own history.

## Forces and Constraints

- External skill repositories are owned elsewhere and change without notice.
- The revision in use has to be recorded in this repository, so that a checkout
  of an old commit here reproduces the skills as they were then.
- Git offers submodules for exactly this, with no extra tooling to build or
  maintain.

## Considered Options

### Git submodules pinned to a revision

Reference each external skill repository as a submodule, so the parent
repository stores the commit SHA of every external repository.

**Pros**
- The pinned revision is recorded in this repository and moves only in an
  explicit commit, which `dc25654` shows was the intended workflow.
- No custom tooling: the mechanism is built into git.
- Checking out an old commit here reproduces the matching external revisions.

**Cons**
- A fresh clone is not usable until `git submodule update --init` has run, a
  cost that `b6590d7` later named explicitly as the reason to undo this
  decision.
- Every revision bump is a commit in this repository, which is visible
  maintenance work.

Alternatives considered at the time were not documented.

## Decision

In the context of consuming skill repositories owned outside this repository,
facing the risk that an upstream change silently alters behaviour here, we
decided for **git submodules pinned to a revision** (inferred from history), to
achieve a reproducible and explicitly recorded external revision, accepting that
a fresh clone needs a submodule init step before it works and that each bump
costs a commit here.

### Consequences

The external revision in use became visible in this repository's history, and
moving it became a deliberate act. `dc25654` is that act performed once.

Cloning the repository stopped being a single step. That cost was carried for
roughly nine months, until DR-0003 traded the pinning away to remove it.

## More Information

Evidence:

- `86354b8` (2023-06-15) — feat: vendored external skills as git submodules to pin their revisions

## Context and Problem Statement

External skills had been consumed as pinned git submodules since 2023-06-15, as
recorded in [DR-0002](DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules.md). A
fresh clone of this repository was therefore incomplete until
`git submodule update --init` had been run, and the history of the external
repositories was pulled into this one.

The commit that made the change states the driving concern in its own subject:
a fresh clone should need no submodule init.

## Forces and Constraints

- A fresh clone should be usable without a submodule step.
- The history of the external repositories should stay out of this repository.
- Whatever replaces submodules has to be a single, repeatable command, since
  the README has to be able to instruct a newcomer in one line.

## Considered Options

### Git submodules pinned to a revision

The arrangement in place since DR-0002.

**Pros**
- Records the exact external revision in this repository's history.
- Built into git, so there is nothing to maintain.

**Cons**
- A fresh clone needs `git submodule update --init` before it works.
- Pulls external history into this repository.

### An auto-cloned sibling checkout

A script, `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh`, clones each external repository
next to this one, and skips any that is already present. The README instructs
the reader to run it once after cloning, and `.gitignore` excludes the
`*-workspace/` directories that result.

**Pros**
- Idempotent: the `[ -d ... ] ||` guard makes a re-run a no-op, so the script is
  safe to run at any time.
- The external history stays in the sibling repositories, out of this one.
- The clone of this repository is complete on its own; the external skills are
  fetched by a plain, readable shell script rather than by submodule mechanics.

**Cons**
- The revision is no longer pinned. The script runs a bare
  `git clone https://example.com/$repo.git` with no ref, so every developer gets
  whatever the default branch holds at the moment they run it. This is the
  guarantee that DR-0002 was written to obtain.
- The post-clone step did not disappear, it changed shape: the README still
  asks the reader to run one command after cloning.
- The external repository list is hard-coded in the script.

## Decision

In the context of external skills consumed as pinned submodules, facing a fresh
clone that did not work until a submodule init had been run, we decided for **an
auto-cloned sibling checkout** (inferred from history) and against **git
submodules**, to achieve a clone that carries none of the external history and a
single idempotent command to fetch it, accepting that the external revision is
no longer pinned and that a manual post-clone step remains.

### Consequences

The repository no longer records which revision of an external skill repository
is in use, so a checkout of an old commit here no longer reproduces the external
skills as they were then. This is a deliberate reversal of DR-0002, and it is
the main risk this decision carries.

Two months later, `70d7483` pinned the markdownlint version in
`.github-linter.json`. The history does not link the two, so the connection is
unverified, but it is the only other pinning in the repository.

## More Information

Evidence:

- `b6590d7` (2024-03-11) — feat: replaced git submodules with an auto-cloned sibling checkout so a fresh clone needs no submodule init
- `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh` — the idempotent clone loop over `community-skills` and `partner-skills`
- `README.md` — "External skills are cloned as sibling repositories. Run `scripts/clone_external_skills.sh` once after a clone."
- `.gitignore` — the `*-workspace/` entry
- No `.gitmodules` remains in the tree

Supersedes [DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules](DR-0002-vendor-external-skills-as-git-submodules.md).
